title: Drum Belt Broken or Dislodged
shortDescription: The dryer drum is not turning at the expected speed.
fullDescription: Midea heat-pump and vented dryers detect drum rotation through a tachometer or current-sensing routine on the drive motor. E30 is set when the drum fails to spin while the motor is energized, almost always caused by a snapped or jumped drive belt.

causes.cause: Idler tensioner pulley failed, slipped belt

symptoms: Motor hums but the drum does not turn
Loud thumping followed by motor running freely
E30 code on the display

fixSteps.title: Verify drum rotation
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door and try to rotate the drum by hand. Excessive resistance indicates a bearing or stuck belt; free rotation suggests a broken belt.

fixSteps.title: Access the cabinet
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer. Remove the top panel screws and the front panel to expose the drum, idler, and motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the drive belt
fixSteps.instruction: Route the new belt around the drum, idler, and motor pulley per the diagram on the inside cabinet. Verify the idler springs back to maintain tension.

whenToCallPro: If the drum bearing is also damaged or you cannot lift the drum out alone.

faq.q: Can I keep using the dryer until I get a new belt?
faq.a: No - running the motor with no load risks overheating the motor coupling.

title: Drum Speed Sensor Error
shortDescription: The drum tachometer is not providing valid pulses.
fullDescription: E31 indicates the speed feedback from the drum sensor is missing or out of range while the motor is commanded to run. Different from E30 (no rotation), E31 can also be triggered by a sensor or harness fault even when the drum is turning.

causes.cause: Magnet on drum pulley fell off

symptoms: Cycle ends prematurely with E31
Drum spins but display shows fault
Motor revs up and down rhythmically before fault

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the cabinet and locate the speed sensor on the motor or drum pulley housing. Reseat the connector and inspect for chafe.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor output
fixSteps.instruction: With the back of the dryer powered, measure the sensor output while spinning the drum by hand. A pulsing voltage indicates a working sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the speed sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the matching Midea sensor and re-clip to the motor housing.

whenToCallPro: If sensor tests good but E31 persists - main board may be at fault.

faq.q: Is E31 the same as E30?
faq.a: Both relate to drum motion, but E30 is no rotation while E31 is no speed feedback signal.

title: Heater Overheat / Thermal Fuse Open
shortDescription: The dryer detected an over-temperature condition in the heating chamber.
fullDescription: E33 is logged when the high-limit thermostat or the thermal fuse opens. On vented dryers this is almost always caused by restricted airflow; on heat-pump models it more often indicates a clogged condenser or evaporator.

causes.cause: Blocked exhaust duct or vent hood

symptoms: Burning or scorched smell during cycle
Cycle stops with E33 within minutes of starting
Drum spins but no heat after fuse opens
Long cycle times even before fault

fixSteps.title: Clean the lint filter
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the lint filter and remove all lint. If the filter has a wax-like film, wash with warm soapy water and dry fully.

fixSteps.title: Clear the vent path
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the exhaust duct from the back of the dryer and inspect the duct and exterior vent hood. Vacuum or brush out lint accumulation.

fixSteps.title: Clean heat-pump filters
fixSteps.instruction: On heat-pump models open the lower service door and rinse the foam pre-filter. Brush the evaporator coil if accessible.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace thermal fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the thermal fuse on the heater or blower housing. Verify continuity; if open, replace and address the airflow root cause.

whenToCallPro: If the dryer continues to overheat after airflow has been restored and parts replaced.

faq.q: Why does the thermal fuse keep blowing?
faq.a: A repeatedly opening fuse is a symptom - the duct or heat-pump system is still restricted.

title: NTC Temperature Sensor Failure
shortDescription: The exhaust or heat-pump NTC sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: E34 indicates the temperature sensor (NTC thermistor) used for cycle control is providing an out-of-range reading. The dryer will not heat or will run a short fault cycle.

causes.cause: Lint blocking the sensor location, allowing condensation damage

symptoms: No heat during the cycle
E34 displayed shortly after start
Cycle finishes early with damp clothes

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the NTC sensor (heater housing on vented; refrigerant line on heat-pump). Reseat the connector.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the NTC and measure resistance at room temperature. Should be approximately 50 kOhm at 25 C. Open or shorted = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the new NTC in the same clip and route harness clear of moving parts.

whenToCallPro: If sensor tests good - the main control board input may be damaged.

faq.q: Will the dryer still spin with E34?
faq.a: Yes, but it will not heat, so clothes will not dry.

title: Door Switch Failure
shortDescription: The dryer door does not register as closed.
fullDescription: E40 is set when the door switch reports open while a cycle is running, or never reports closed when start is pressed. The dryer will not start or will pause until the switch reads closed.
symptoms: Cycle pauses repeatedly mid-run
Start button does nothing despite display being lit
E40 on display

fixSteps.title: Inspect the door catch
fixSteps.instruction: Open and close the door and verify the latch hits the strike squarely. Adjust by tightening the strike screw if loose.

fixSteps.title: Test the switch
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the harness and use a multimeter to check continuity as the actuator is pressed. Replace if stuck.

fixSteps.title: Replace the door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top panel to access the switch, install the new switch, and reconnect the harness.

faq.q: Can I bypass the door switch?
faq.a: No - the door switch is a safety device, never bypass it.

title: Drive Motor Fault
shortDescription: The drum drive motor failed to start or stalled during operation.
fullDescription: E50 covers electrical faults of the drive motor. The control senses excessive current draw, low current with no rotation, or stalled motor on Midea inverter-driven dryers.

causes.cause: Seized drum (lint or foreign object jamming the drum)

symptoms: Motor hum then E50
Cycle stops within seconds of pressing start
Burning smell from the motor area

fixSteps.title: Verify free rotation
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, rotate the drum by hand. Bind = mechanical issue; free = electrical.

fixSteps.title: Check capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge the run capacitor, then measure capacitance. A reading well below the rated uF means a failed cap.

fixSteps.title: Test motor windings
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the motor and measure resistance across the windings. Open or shorted = replace motor.

fixSteps.title: Replace the motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install the matching Midea drive motor, transfer the pulley, and re-tension the belt.

whenToCallPro: Most users should call a pro - motor replacement requires full cabinet disassembly.

faq.q: Can the inverter board cause E50?
faq.a: Yes - on inverter heat-pump models a failed driver stage produces the same symptom as a bad motor.

title: Compressor Fault (Heat-Pump Models)
shortDescription: The heat-pump compressor failed to start or is drawing abnormal current.
fullDescription: E54 is specific to Midea heat-pump dryers. The control monitors compressor current and discharge temperature; protection trips if the compressor stalls, overheats, or loses charge.

causes.cause: Compressor overheat - blocked airflow on the condenser

symptoms: Long cycle times before fault appears
Lukewarm exhaust
E54 after a few minutes of running
Clicking from the compressor area without a steady hum

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser air path
fixSteps.instruction: Open the lower service panel, remove the foam pre-filter, and rinse. Vacuum the evaporator/condenser coils.

fixSteps.title: Allow cool-down
fixSteps.instruction: Leave the dryer unplugged for 2 hours so the internal protector resets, then retest.

fixSteps.title: Test start capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure the start cap on the compressor. Replace if out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Refrigerant diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If E54 persists, a refrigeration tech is required to recover, evacuate, and recharge the sealed system.

whenToCallPro: Sealed-system work always requires a refrigeration-licensed technician.
videoSearchQuery: Midea heat pump dryer E54 compressor

faq.a: No - refrigerant work is regulated and requires recovery equipment.

title: Water Tank Full
shortDescription: The condensate water tank is full and must be emptied.
fullDescription: Heat-pump and condenser dryers collect condensed moisture in a removable tank. E60 (often shown alongside a tank icon) indicates the float switch in the tank reservoir is reporting full.

causes.cause: Drain pump not pumping water from sump to tank or to drain hose
Failed reed switch in the tank seat

symptoms: E60 with the water tank icon flashing
Water visible in the drum after a cycle
Drying time abnormally long before fault

fixSteps.title: Empty the water tank
fixSteps.instruction: Slide the tank out of the upper compartment, pour the water down a drain, and reseat firmly until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Free the float
fixSteps.instruction: Open the tank cap and gently work the float up and down to ensure it moves freely. Rinse with warm water.

fixSteps.title: Test the drain pump
fixSteps.instruction: If water collects in the sump, listen for the drain pump priming. Remove and clean the pump impeller of lint.

fixSteps.title: Use direct drain hose
fixSteps.instruction: If permitted by your model, connect the optional drain hose to a standpipe to bypass the tank entirely.

whenToCallPro: If the drain pump assembly cannot be cleared.

faq.q: Can I keep running the dryer if I empty the tank?
faq.a: Yes - emptying after every cycle is normal for condenser/heat-pump dryers.

title: Communication Error Between Boards
shortDescription: User interface and main control board are not communicating.
fullDescription: E72 indicates the main board lost serial contact with the display board. The unit cannot accept inputs and will refuse to start or will halt mid-cycle.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable between display and main board
Surge damage to the UI MCU

symptoms: Buttons unresponsive
E72 on display, sometimes flickering
Cycle does not start

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer for 5 minutes. Many E72 events are transient.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the top panel and reseat the cable between display and main board. Inspect for bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI display
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating fails, replace the user interface board.

whenToCallPro: If the main control board appears to be the cause.

faq.q: Could a power surge cause this?
faq.a: Yes - surges commonly damage the lower-power MCU on the display board.

title: Supply Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Mains voltage is too high or too low for safe operation.
fullDescription: EH0 (sometimes shown as E80) is reported when the main board detects line voltage outside the safe operating window for several seconds. Heating and motor power-stages are inhibited until voltage returns to spec.

causes.cause: Brownout or sag on the local utility
Loose neutral on the household circuit
Failed input filter on the main board

symptoms: EH0 appears, sometimes intermittently
Lights in the home dim when other appliances cycle
Cycle aborts shortly after start

fixSteps.title: Plug directly into a wall outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Remove any extension cord or power strip and plug the dryer directly into a properly rated outlet.

fixSteps.title: Measure outlet voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With a multimeter, verify the outlet reads within +/-10% of rated (120 V or 230 V depending on region) under load.

fixSteps.title: Have circuit inspected
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is out of spec, an electrician should inspect the breaker and shared neutral.

whenToCallPro: If the home circuit is suspect, an electrician is required.

faq.q: Will a surge protector fix EH0?
faq.a: No - EH0 is about voltage range, not transients. Address the underlying supply.
